exposes.$comment: VAPP-180 (the format half of the eMCP contract, packages/emcp fixtures/exposes.json in the Exponential repo): `exposes: [{name, title, description, input, access, run}]` = MCP tools a host's broker lists (as `<app>__<name>`) and runs as the CALLING person, data never code. `name` matches `limits.namePattern`, at most `limits.nameMax`, never holds `limits.separator`, unique; `title` (at most titleMax) and `description` (at most descriptionMax) non-blank; `input` = a JSON Schema `{type: "object", properties?}`; `access` read | write; at most `limits.maxTools` tools. `run` holds EXACTLY ONE of `runKinds`: `records: {op, kind, id?, where?, data?, limit?}` over the package's OWN kinds (op in `recordOps`; `readRecordOps` read, upsert writes; a delete is destructive and refused); `action` (+ `args`) = a host function name matching `actionPattern` (it reads when the last word of its name is a `readOpWords` word, else it writes); `upstream` (+ `tool`, `args`) = one of the package's `upstreams` (the MCP server names the HOST provides: Exponential = the team's MCP servers); `agent` (+ `prompt`, `device?`) hands the input to one of the host's agents by slug (matching `agent.slugPattern`, at most `agent.slugMax`, else `agent`): `prompt` non-blank, at most `agent.promptMax` characters (else `prompt`), `device` absent or one of `agent.devices` (else `run`); it always writes (Exponential: a team agent through `sessions_send`, #VAPP-236). Every string of `run` may hold `${input.<dotted path>}` templates whose first key is a declared input property. Destructive is never exposed: an action or upstream tool whose name holds a `destructiveWords` word (words = the `_`-separated words) is refused. A binding declared read whose run writes is refused; an upstream tool's level is its live annotations', checked by the host at call. Issues come in binding order with the eMCP error code (`exposeIssues`). What a run may reach on a given host (which actions exist and are grantable, destructive arguments, which upstreams the team has) is the host's own check on top.
